subject: maths
title: Line Graphs, Tables and Timetables
seo_title: Year 5 Line Graphs and Tables Worksheets: Two-Way Tables and Timetables (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Solve comparison, sum and difference problems using information presented in a line graph; complete, read and interpret information in tables, including timetables.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on line graphs and tables: read scales and values between grid lines, compare two lines, complete two-way tables and use 24-hour bus and train timetables. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Check the scale first. Then read across, up or down carefully.
key_sub: Work out what one small square is worth. Sum means add; difference means subtract. In a table, find the row, then the column. For journey times, count on to the next hour: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.
body_html:
Read a line graph

A line graph shows how something changes, often over time. First check the scale. Count the small squares between two labels and work out what one square is worth. Then go up from the bottom axis to the line, and across to the scale.

Some points sit between two grid lines. If a point is halfway between 10 and 12, it shows 11.

Compare two lines

When a graph has two lines, check the key to see which line is which. Sum questions (altogether, in total) mean add. Difference questions (how many more, how much warmer) mean subtract.

Example 1

How much warmer was Cardiff than Glasgow in April?

April: Cardiff 12 °C, Glasgow 8 °C. Difference: 12 − 8 = 4.

Answer: 4 °C

Read and complete a two-way table

A two-way table sorts data in two ways at once. Find the row first, then go across to the column. The Total row and Total column help you find a missing number.

5A5BTotal
Walk16?35
Car121123
Total283058
Example 2

How many pupils in 5B walk to school?

The Walk row adds up to 35. 5A is 16. So 5B is 35 − 16 = 19. Check the 5B column: 19 + 11 = 30.

Answer: 19 pupils

Read a timetable

A timetable uses the 24-hour clock. Each column is one bus or train. Go down a column to follow one journey. A dash (—) means it does not stop there.

Example 3

How long does Bus 1 take from the Town Hall to the Station?

Count on to the next hour: 13:40 to 14:00 is 20 minutes, 14:00 to 14:15 is 15 minutes. 20 + 15 = 35.

Answer: 35 minutes

Do not take away the times like ordinary numbers: 1415 − 1340 = 75 is wrong, because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting each small square as 1Work out the scale: 5 squares between 0 and 10 means 2 each
Reading a point between grid lines as the line belowHalfway between 600 and 700 is 650
Reading the graph at the wrong timeGo straight up from the time on the bottom axis
Using the wrong line on a graph with two linesCheck the key: solid or dashed
Adding when the question asks how many moreHow many more, how much warmer: subtract
Mixing up rows and columns in a tableRow first, then go across to the column
Taking away times as if an hour had 100 minutesCount on to the next hour, then add the minutes

faq.q: What statistics do children learn in Year 5?
faq.a: In Year 5 pupils solve comparison, sum and difference problems using line graphs, and they complete, read and interpret tables, including timetables. This builds on the bar charts and time graphs from Year 4.

faq.q: How do you read a line graph in Year 5?
faq.a: Check what each small square on the scale is worth, then go up from the bottom axis to the line and across to the scale. If the point is halfway between two grid lines, the value is halfway between them too.

faq.q: How do you work out journey times on a timetable?
faq.a: Find the start and end times in the same column, then count on: first to the next hour, then the extra minutes. From 14:38 to 15:41 is 22 + 41 = 63 minutes, or 1 hour 3 minutes.
A two-way table sorts data by two things at once, such as class and lunch choice. Read across a row and down a column to find a cell, and use the totals to work out any missing numbers.

items.q: On the temperature scale, what is each small square worth?
items.e: The labels go 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. There are 5 small squares between two labels. 5 ÷ 5 = 1, so each small square is 1 °C.

items.q: What was the temperature at 10:00?
items.e: Go up from 10:00 to the point, then across to the scale. It is 1 small square above 10, so 11 °C.

items.q: What was the highest temperature?
items.e: The highest point is at 14:00. It is 3 small squares above 15, so 18 °C. (20 °C is the top of the scale, not a reading.)

items.q: What was the lowest temperature?
items.e: The lowest point is at 06:00. It is 4 small squares above 0, so 4 °C. (6 is the time, 06:00, not the temperature.)

items.q: At what time was the temperature 13 °C?
items.e: Find 13 on the scale (3 small squares above 10). Go across to the line and down: 16:00.

items.q: On the distance scale, what is each small square worth?
items.e: The labels go up in 200s. There are 2 small squares between two labels, so each square is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 m.

items.q: How far from home was Freya at 10:20?
items.e: At 10:20 the point is halfway between the lines for 600 and 700, so 650 m.

items.q: The park is the furthest point from home on Freya’s walk. How far from home is the park?
items.e: The highest part of the line is at 900 m (1 small square below 1,000). (1,800 m is there and back.)

items.q: Freya stopped at the park. When was she at the park?
items.e: When Freya stops, her distance from home does not change, so the line is flat. From 10:30 to 10:40 it stays at 900 m.

items.q: At 11:00 the line is back at 0 m. What does this mean?
items.e: The graph shows the distance from home. 0 m from home means Freya is at home again. She walked to the park and back.

items.q: How tall was the bean plant in week 2?
items.e: The labels go up in 10s and each small square is 2 cm. In week 2 the point is halfway between the lines for 10 and 12, so 11 cm.

items.q: In which week was the plant 24 cm tall?
items.e: Find 24 on the scale: 2 small squares above 20. Go across to the line and down: week 4.

items.q: How tall was the plant in week 5?
items.e: In week 5 the point is halfway between the lines for 28 and 30, so 29 cm.

items.q: In which week was the plant first taller than 20 cm?
items.e: In week 3 it was 18 cm, which is not taller than 20 cm. In week 4 it was 24 cm, so week 4 is the first.

items.q: How tall was the plant when it was first measured, in week 0?
items.e: Week 0 is the first point. It is halfway between the lines for 2 and 4, so 3 cm. (The plant was already 3 cm tall, not 0 cm.)

items.q: What was the temperature of the hot chocolate after 5 minutes?
items.e: The labels go up in 20s, so each small square is 10 °C. At 5 minutes the point is halfway between 60 and 70: 65 °C.

items.q: After how many minutes was the hot chocolate 40 °C?
items.e: Find 40 on the temperature scale, go across to the line, then down to the minutes: 20 minutes.

items.q: What was the temperature after 15 minutes?
items.e: At 15 minutes the point is halfway between 40 and 50, so 45 °C. (15 is the time, not the temperature.)

items.q: When was the hot chocolate cooling fastest?
items.e: Fastest means the steepest part of the line. From 0 to 5 minutes it fell 80 − 65 = 15 °C. In every other 5 minutes it fell 10 °C or less.

items.q: Between which two times did the temperature fall the most?
items.e: The line goes down after 14:00. 14:00 to 16:00: 18 − 13 = 5 °C. 16:00 to 18:00: 13 − 9 = 4 °C. So it fell most from 14:00 to 16:00. (10:00 to 12:00 is the biggest rise, not a fall.)

sets.title: Compare two lines: sum and difference

items.q: How many books did Year 5 borrow in week 2?
items.e: Year 5 is the solid line with round dots. Each small square is 2 books. In week 2 the dot is halfway between 30 and 32, so 31. (26 is the dashed Year 6 line.)

items.q: How many books were borrowed altogether in week 5?
items.e: Week 5: Year 5 42, Year 6 29. Altogether means add: 42 + 29 = 71.

items.q: How many more books did Year 6 borrow than Year 5 in week 6?
items.e: Week 6: Year 6 45, Year 5 38. How many more means subtract: 45 − 38 = 7.

items.q: In which week did both year groups borrow the same number of books?
items.e: Look for the place where the two lines meet. In week 4 both are on 36.

items.q: How many books did Year 6 borrow in weeks 1 and 2 altogether?
items.e: Use the dashed Year 6 line: week 1 30, week 2 26. 30 + 26 = 56. (55 uses the Year 5 line.)

items.q: In how many of the weeks did Year 6 borrow more books than Year 5?
items.e: The dashed line is above the solid line in weeks 1, 3 and 6. In week 4 they are the same, so it does not count.

items.q: How much warmer was Bristol than Aberdeen in May?
items.e: May: Bristol 13 °C, Aberdeen 10 °C. How much warmer means find the difference: 13 − 10 = 3 °C.

items.q: In which month was the difference between the two cities the biggest?
items.e: Find the biggest gap between the lines. June: 16 − 12 = 4 °C. Every other month the gap is 2 °C or 3 °C. (July is the warmest month, but the gap is only 18 − 15 = 3 °C.)

items.q: By how much did the temperature in Aberdeen rise from January to July?
items.e: Use the dashed Aberdeen line. January: 3 °C. July: 15 °C. 15 − 3 = 12 °C. (13 °C is the Bristol line.)

items.q: In which month was the temperature in Aberdeen 10 °C?
items.e: Find 10 on the scale and go across to the dashed Aberdeen line: May. (Bristol, the solid line, was 10 °C in April.)

items.q: Whose sunflower was taller in week 4, and by how much?
items.e: Each small square is 10 cm. Week 4: Poppy 70 cm, Jack 60 cm. Poppy’s is taller: 70 − 60 = 10 cm.

items.q: Jack’s sunflower was taller at the start. In which week was it taller than Poppy’s again?
items.e: From week 2 to week 5 the solid Poppy line is above. In week 6 the dashed Jack line is on top: 100 cm against 95 cm.

items.q: How much did Poppy’s sunflower grow from week 2 to week 5?
items.e: Poppy (solid line): week 2 35 cm, week 5 85 cm. 85 − 35 = 50 cm. (40 cm is Jack’s line.)

items.q: In which week was the difference between the two sunflowers the biggest?
items.e: Find the biggest gap between the lines. Week 5: 85 − 70 = 15 cm. Week 4: 10 cm. Week 6: 5 cm. (Week 6 has the tallest sunflower, not the biggest gap.)

items.q: What was the total height of both sunflowers in week 6?
items.e: Week 6: Poppy 95 cm (halfway between 90 and 100), Jack 100 cm. Total means add: 95 + 100 = 195 cm.

items.q: How far had Isla walked by 15:45?
items.e: Use the solid Isla line. Each small square is 100 m. At 15:45 the dot is halfway between 700 and 800: 750 m.

items.q: How far apart were Isla and Leo at 15:40?
items.e: 15:40: Leo 1,200 m, Isla 500 m. The distance between them is the difference: 1,200 − 500 = 700 m.

items.q: How much further had Leo travelled than Isla at 15:50?
Leo stopped at a shop on the way. For how long did he stop?
items.e: The Leo line is flat from 15:40 to 15:50. That is 10 minutes. (The dots are 5 minutes apart, and the flat part covers 2 gaps.)

items.q: The park is 1,800 m from school. How much further did Isla still have to walk at 16:00?
items.e: At 16:00 Isla had walked 1,500 m. 1,800 − 1,500 = 300 m still to walk.

sets.title: Read and complete tables and two-way tables

items.q: How many pupils in 5B have a packed lunch?
items.e: Find the Packed lunch row, then go across to the 5B column: 9. (11 is 5A.)

items.q: How many pupils in 5A have a school dinner?
items.e: School dinner row, 5A column: 14.

items.q: How many pupils are in 5A?
items.e: The Total row at the bottom gives each class. 5A: 14 + 11 + 3 = 28.

items.q: How many more pupils have a school dinner than a packed lunch?
items.e: Use the Total column. School dinner: 31. Packed lunch: 20. 31 − 20 = 11. (Using only one class gives 3 or 8.)

items.q: How many pupils are in Year 5 altogether?
items.e: The bottom right cell is the total of everything: 28 + 30 = 58 pupils.

items.q: What time does the swimming pool close on Saturday?
items.e: Find the Saturday row, then go across to the Closes column: 17:30 (5:30 pm).

items.q: How long is the pool open on Sunday?
items.e: 09:30 to 15:30 is 6 hours. 15:30 to 16:00 is 30 minutes. So the pool is open 6 hours 30 minutes. (1600 − 930 = 670 treats an hour as 100 minutes.)

items.q: On which day is the pool open for the longest time?
items.e: Work out each day: Monday 13 hours 30 minutes, Wednesday 15 hours, Saturday 9 hours 30 minutes, Sunday 6 hours 30 minutes. Wednesday is the longest. (Monday opens just as early, but closes earlier.)

items.q: How far is it by road from Birmingham to Leeds?
items.e: Find the Birmingham row and go across to the Leeds column: 195 km. You get the same number from the Leeds row and the Birmingham column.

items.q: Which two cities are the closest?
items.e: Find the smallest number in the table: 70 km, between Manchester and Leeds.

items.q: Mohammed drives from London to Birmingham, then from Birmingham to Manchester. How far does he drive?
items.e: London to Birmingham: 190 km. Birmingham to Manchester: 140 km. 190 + 140 = 330 km. (335 km is the straight road from London to Manchester.)

items.q: How much further is it from London to Manchester than from London to Leeds?
items.e: London row: Manchester 335 km, Leeds 315 km. 335 − 315 = 20 km. (70 km is from Manchester to Leeds.)

items.q: How many adult tickets were sold on Friday?
items.e: The adult row adds up to 183. Thursday is 86. 183 − 86 = 97 tickets. Check: 86 + 97 = 183.

items.q: How many child tickets were sold altogether?
items.e: Add along the Child row: 124 + 158 = 282. Remember to exchange: 4 + 8 = 12 ones.

items.q: What number is missing from the table?
items.e: The bottom right cell is the total of all tickets. Add the Total column: 183 + 282 = 465. Check with the Total row: 210 + 255 = 465.

items.q: On which day were more child tickets sold, and how many more?
items.e: Child row: Thursday 124, Friday 158. Friday is more: 158 − 124 = 34.

items.q: How many boys cannot swim 25 m?
items.e: There are 45 boys. 38 of them can swim. 45 − 38 = 7 boys cannot.

items.q: How many pupils can swim 25 m?
items.e: Add down the Can column: 38 + 41 = 79. (92 is everyone in Year 5, and 13 is the Cannot column.)

items.q: How many pupils are in Year 5 altogether?
items.e: Add the Total column: 45 + 47 = 92. 5 + 7 = 12 ones, so exchange 10 ones for 1 ten. Check with the Total row: 79 + 13 = 92.

items.q: How many pupils come to school by bus?
items.e: Add the numbers you know: 23 + 14 + 8 + 5 = 50. The total is 60, so 60 − 50 = 10 pupils come by bus.

items.q: The bus leaves the Bus Station at 09:15. What time does it get to the Hospital?
items.e: Find 09:15 in the Bus Station row. Go down that column (Bus 2) to the Hospital row: 09:49.

items.q: Which bus does not stop at the Library?
items.e: A dash (—) means the bus does not stop there. The dash in the Library row is in the Bus 3 column.

items.q: How long does Bus 1 take from the Bus Station to the Retail Park?
items.e: 08:45 to 09:00 is 15 minutes. 09:00 to 09:32 is 32 minutes. 15 + 32 = 47 minutes. (87 minutes uses 100 minutes in an hour.)

items.q: How long does Bus 1 take from the High Street to the Library?
items.e: High Street 08:58, Library 09:06. 08:58 to 09:06 is 8 minutes.

items.q: Arjun gets to the High Street at 09:31, just after a bus has left. How long must he wait for the next bus?
items.e: The bus at 09:28 has gone. The next bus at the High Street is at 09:58. From 09:31 to 09:58 is 27 minutes.

items.q: How long does it take to go from the High Street to the Hospital?
items.e: Use any bus that stops at both. Bus 2: High Street 09:28, Hospital 09:49. 09:28 to 09:49 is 21 minutes.

items.q: Zara must be at the Hospital by 10:30. What is the latest bus she can catch from the Bus Station?
items.e: Look along the Hospital row for the last time before 10:30: 10:19. Go up that column to the Bus Station: 09:45. The next bus gets to the Hospital at 10:49, which is too late.

items.q: Grace gets to the Library at 09:52. How long must she wait for a bus?
items.e: Bus 3 does not stop at the Library (—). So the next bus there is Bus 4 at 10:36. 09:52 to 10:00 is 8 minutes, 10:00 to 10:36 is 36 minutes: 8 + 36 = 44 minutes.

items.q: Bus 1 is 10 minutes late at every stop. What time does it get to the Library?
items.e: On the timetable Bus 1 gets to the Library at 09:06. 10 minutes later is 09:16.

items.q: How many buses get to the Hospital before 10:00?
items.e: Hospital row: 09:19, 09:49, 10:19, 10:49. Only 09:19 and 09:49 are before 10:00, so 2 buses.

items.q: How long does Train 1 take from Westbrook to Northgate?
items.e: 14:38 to 15:00 is 22 minutes. 15:00 to 15:41 is 41 minutes. 22 + 41 = 63 minutes = 1 hour 3 minutes. (103 minutes takes 1541 − 1438 as if an hour had 100 minutes.)

items.q: Which train is the quickest from Westbrook to Northgate?
items.e: Train 2 takes 48 minutes. The others take 1 hour 3 minutes. Train 2 is quicker because it does not stop at Millford or Ashby Road.

items.q: How much quicker is Train 2 than Train 1 from Westbrook to Northgate?
items.e: Train 1 takes 63 minutes and Train 2 takes 48 minutes. 63 − 48 = 15 minutes.

items.q: Which trains stop at Millford?
items.e: Look along the Millford row. Train 2 has a dash (—), so it does not stop. Trains 1, 3 and 4 stop.

items.q: Noah’s train gets to Kingsley at 4:49 pm. Which time on the timetable is this?
items.e: 4:49 pm is in the afternoon, so add 12 to the hour: 4 + 12 = 16. Look for 16:49 in the Kingsley row.

items.q: Maya gets to Ashby Road station at 15:12. How long must she wait for the next train?
items.e: Train 2 does not stop at Ashby Road (—). The next train there is Train 3 at 16:05. 15:12 to 16:00 is 48 minutes, then 5 more minutes: 48 + 5 = 53 minutes.

items.q: Leo must be in Northgate by 16:45. What is the latest train he can catch from Westbrook?
items.e: Northgate row: the last time before 16:45 is 16:41 (Train 3). Go up to Westbrook: 15:38. Train 4 gets in at 17:11, too late.

items.q: How long does Train 3 take from Millford to Kingsley?
items.e: 15:52 to 16:00 is 8 minutes. 16:00 to 16:19 is 19 minutes. 8 + 19 = 27 minutes. (Not 67: an hour has 60 minutes.)

items.q: Train 4 is 12 minutes late. What time does it get to Northgate?
items.e: Train 4 should get to Northgate at 17:11. 17:11 + 12 minutes: 11 + 12 = 23, so 17:23.

items.q: How long is it between Train 1 and Train 3 leaving Westbrook?
items.e: 14:38 to 15:38 is exactly 1 hour (60 minutes). The minutes are the same and the hour goes up by 1. (100 minutes takes 1538 − 1438 as if an hour had 100 minutes.)

sets.title: Word problems with graphs, tables and timetables

items.q: After week 6, the bean plant grows 3 cm every week. In which week will it first be taller than 40 cm?
items.e: Week 6: 32 cm. Week 7: 35 cm. Week 8: 38 cm (not taller than 40 cm yet). Week 9: 41 cm.

items.q: Mum and her two children buy return tickets. How much do they pay altogether?
items.e: Adult return £4.20. Two child returns: 2 × £2.10 = £4.20. £4.20 + £4.20 = £8.40.

items.q: How much does a child save by buying a return ticket instead of two single tickets?
Year 5 want to borrow 250 books in these 6 weeks. How many more books do they need to borrow?
Kai catches Train 3. From Northgate station he walks for 12 minutes to the football stadium. What time does he get to the stadium?
items.e: Train 3 gets to Northgate at 16:41. 16:41 + 12 minutes = 16:53.

items.q: Mohammed drives from Leeds to London and back again. How far does he drive?
items.e: Leeds to London is 315 km. There and back is 2 × 315 = 630 km.

items.q: Amelia waits until her hot chocolate is below 50 °C. After how many minutes is it first below 50 °C?
items.e: At 10 minutes it is 55 °C, which is not below 50 °C. At 15 minutes it is 45 °C, so 15 minutes.

items.q: A school dinner costs £2.50. How much do the pupils in 5B pay for school dinners in one day?
Adult tickets cost £4 and child tickets cost £2. How much money did Thursday’s tickets make?
Lily gets to the swimming pool at 16:20 on Saturday. How long can she swim before it closes?
items.e: Saturday closes at 17:30. 16:20 to 17:00 is 40 minutes, 17:00 to 17:30 is 30 minutes. 40 + 30 = 70 minutes.

items.q: Ethan gets on the bus at the Library. He must be at the Retail Park by 10:15. What is the latest bus he can catch from the Library?
items.e: Retail Park row: 10:02 gets there before 10:15. That is Bus 2, which leaves the Library at 09:36. Bus 3 gets there at 10:32, which is too late (and it does not stop at the Library).

items.q: How many more girls than boys can swim 25 m?
items.e: Can column: girls 41, boys 38. 41 − 38 = 3. (2 uses the Total column, not the Can column.)

items.q: How long did Leo take to get from school to the park, including his stop?
items.e: Leo leaves at 15:30 and reaches 1,800 m at 15:55. 15:30 to 15:55 is 25 minutes. The 10-minute stop is part of the journey.

items.q: Poppy says, “My sunflower grew more than Jack’s from week 0 to week 6.” Is she right?
items.e: Poppy: 95 − 10 = 85 cm. Jack: 100 − 15 = 85 cm. They grew the same amount. (95 cm and 100 cm are the heights, not how much they grew.)

items.q: For how many of the months shown was Bristol 10 °C or warmer?
items.e: Bristol (solid line): April 10 °C, May 13 °C, June 16 °C, July 18 °C. That is 4 months. 10 °C counts, because it says 10 °C or warmer.

items.q: A lorry drives from Manchester to Leeds and back 3 times every day. How far does it drive each day?
items.e: One trip there and back: 2 × 70 = 140 km. 3 trips: 3 × 140 = 420 km.

items.q: Ava takes Train 1 from Westbrook to Kingsley. She stays in Kingsley for 1 hour 20 minutes, then catches the next train to Northgate. What time does she get to Northgate?
items.e: Train 1 gets to Kingsley at 15:19. 1 hour 20 minutes later is 16:39. The next train at Kingsley is Train 4 at 16:49. It gets to Northgate at 17:11.

items.q: Half of the pupils who come by car start walking to school instead. How many pupils walk now?
items.e: Half of 14 is 7. These pupils join the 23 who already walk: 23 + 7 = 30.

items.q: How much did the bean plant grow from week 3 to week 6?
items.e: Week 3: 18 cm. Week 6: 32 cm. Growth is the difference: 32 − 18 = 14 cm.

items.q: At what time was the temperature half of the temperature at 14:00?
items.e: At 14:00 it was 18 °C. Half of 18 is 9. The temperature was 9 °C at 18:00.
